method: Computes median path loss with the Okumura-Hata equations, or the COST-231 Hata extension for 1500–2000 MHz. Inputs are the model, the environment, the frequency in MHz, the base and mobile antenna heights in metres and the distance in kilometres. Okumura-Hata evaluates 69.55 + 26.16 log10(f) − 13.82 log10(h_b) − a(h_m) + (44.9 − 6.55 log10(h_b)) log10(d). The mobile correction a(h_m) is (1.1 log10 f − 0.7) h_m − (1.56 log10 f − 0.8) for a medium–small city, 8.29 (log10 1.54 h_m)² − 1.1 for a large city at 200 MHz and below, and 3.2 (log10 11.75 h_m)² − 4.97 for a large city at 400 MHz and above, with the 400 MHz form applied in the 200–400 MHz gap that Hata leaves undefined. In the Okumura-Hata model, suburban paths then take the medium-city loss less 2 (log10(f/28))² + 5.4 dB, and open or rural paths take it less 4.78 (log10 f)² − 18.33 log10 f + 40.94 dB, both using the medium-city mobile correction. COST-231 Hata replaces the constant with 46.3 and the frequency term with 33.9 log10 f, keeps the same base-height and distance terms and the medium-city a(h_m), and adds C_m = 3 dB for a dense urban centre and 0 dB for a medium city or a suburb; it defines no open-area form, so that combination is refused rather than extrapolated. Inputs are refused outside the fitted ranges: 150–1500 MHz for Okumura-Hata, 1500–2000 MHz for COST-231, base height 30–200 m, mobile height 1–10 m and distance 1–20 km. The result reports the median loss, the mobile correction, the distance slope in dB per decade, the free-space loss over the same path and the excess above it, and lists the additive terms so the arithmetic can be checked by hand. Predictions are medians: terrain profiles, buildings, foliage, building penetration, antenna patterns, feeder loss and site height above the clutter are not modelled, and microcells, indoor paths and street canyons fall outside the models' assumptions. Pure local arithmetic: no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: ITU-R P.529, Prediction methods for the terrestrial land mobile service in the VHF and UHF bands — the Hata and COST-231 formulations and their fitted ranges.
ITU-R P.1546, Method for point-to-area predictions for terrestrial services in the frequency range 30 MHz to 4000 MHz — the wider prediction framework these models sit in.
M. Hata, Empirical formula for propagation loss in land mobile radio services, IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology, 1980 — the paper that fitted the equations to Okumura's measurements.
